build_turbopack.note: Fails in this session with TurbopackInternalError: 'creating new process / binding to a port / Operation not permitted (os error 1)' inside Turbopack's PostCSS worker, both with and without this session's own command sandbox disabled (dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true) — ruling out Claude Code's own sandbox as the cause. A plain Node http server binds a local port successfully in the same shell, so this is specific to whatever child-process Turbopack's CSS loader spawns on this host. B001 and B002 both reported a clean `npm run build` (see their TEST_RESULTS.json); this is a newly observed environment limitation in this session, not a regression introduced by any B003 code change (confirmed: no B003 commit touches next.config, postcss config, or any CSS). Not claimed as PASS.

build_webpack_fallback.note: Webpack compiles the application successfully in 8.5s (confirms the Turbopack failure above is tooling/environment, not a code defect), but Next's own generated-route-type-check step then fails on a PRE-EXISTING, unrelated issue: app/api/live/route.ts exports a non-handler helper (`runLiveAction`) that Next 16's typed-route validation rejects. Confirmed pre-existing via `git log -1 -- app/api/live/route.ts` (last touched by an unrelated migration-rename commit, not any B001/B002/B003 commit) and via `git diff --stat` showing zero B003 changes to that file. Recorded as a known, pre-existing, untouched-by-this-project issue, not fixed in B003 (out of this batch's authorized scope — items 1 and 2 only touch the dismiss button/context-threading and its test file).

new_or_changed_test_files.kind: real-guard integration (DB mocked, auth/role logic real) — dismiss against a real existing broadcast row, 5 identities x 1 route + 3 edge cases

mock_fix.finding: Codex B002 review (standards section): the display_type_state/display_state .then() handlers used `row ?? {defaults}` on UPDATE, which could fabricate a row that should not exist.
mock_fix.fix: removed the `??` fallback; the mock now only mutates a row if it already exists, matching real SQL UPDATE semantics (an absent row stays absent).
mock_fix.verification: app/api/display-engine/owner-floor-matrix.test.ts full suite re-run after the fix: 23/23 pass.

dismiss_matrix_added.finding: Codex B002 review: the only existing dismiss test used a nonexistent broadcast id, which 404s before role authorization ever runs — 'that test would pass before the owner-floor fix too.'
dismiss_matrix_added.fix: added a real `display_broadcasts` table case to the mock (select/update with id+event_id filter tracking), seeded a real existing broadcast row in beforeEach, and added a 5-identity x real-broadcast matrix plus 3 explicitly-labeled 'not role tests' edge cases (nonexistent id, wrong event, missing eventId).
dismiss_matrix_added.result: owner succeeds with exactly one scoped write and a non-null dismissed_at; every denied identity leaves zero writes and the broadcast row byte-unchanged.

live_verification.reason: Item 1 (role-aware Dismiss button) and item 2 (real-broadcast test matrix) were verified at the unit-test layer in this batch, per repository_checks and new_or_changed_test_files above. New live-browser rendered-UI evidence for the Dismiss button's three states (owner-enabled, non-owner-disabled-with-tooltip, token-absent) was not captured in B003 — see BATCH_REPORT.md 'Remaining gaps' for why, and the new fixtures/owner_floor_live_matrix.mjs script prepared for a future batch to use.
